findings.evidence: §4.6, 'Memory planning' bullet: "The architecture must therefore limit concurrency, quantize KV (FP8 → ~1.31 MB/token, ~12.06 GB/request at the same 9,200-token context), or use a GQA architecture. ... a GQA model (8 KV-heads, d_head=128) would carry only ~0.33 MB/token, ~8× less figure (Ch 7)."
findings.issue: Broken/garbled phrase: '~8× less figure' is not grammatical and has no referent — the intended statement is that the per-token KV constant is ~8× smaller than the 2.62 MB/token full-MHA figure. This sits in the load-bearing 'Memory planning' bullet that decides the KV budget for the canonical workload, and the same construction ('~8× less figure') appears in the immediately preceding sentence of the same bullet, so a reader cannot resolve what is being compared. The arithmetic itself is correct (2×80×(8×128)×2 B = 327,680 B ≈ 0.33 MB/token ≈ 2.62/8, matching Ch 5 §5.3(b) and Ch 7 §7.3).
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the two affected sentences in §4.6's 'Memory planning' bullet as: '... or use a GQA architecture: a GQA model (8 KV-heads, head_dim 128) would carry only ~0.33 MB/token, ~8× less than the ~2.62 MB/token full-MHA figure (Ch 7).' and '... quantize KV (FP8 → ~1.31 MB/token, ~12.06 GB/request at the same 9,200-token context, i.e. ~8× less than the ~24.1 GB FP16 figure, Ch 7) ...'. Sweep the chapter and Ch 7 for the same truncated '... less figure' construction.

findings.evidence: One host's 436 GB KV budget holds 17.5 slots... floored to 17.
findings.issue: Arithmetic check: 436 GB / 24.9 GB/slot = 17.51. The book floors this to 17 slots for conservative sizing. 17 * 24.9 = 423.3 GB, which fits within 436 GB. 18 * 24.9 = 448.2 GB, which exceeds 436 GB. The flooring logic is correct.
